title: Inference SLO‑aligned metrics muxer and OTLP→Prometheus normalizer
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Summary:
We need a single ingestion component ("metrics muxer") that canonicalizes incoming OTLP metrics and Prometheus scrape data for inference workloads, enriches them with inference-specific labels, and emits Prometheus-friendly metrics and derived KPIs aligned to SLOs (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, tokens_per_second). This ticket implements the OTLP→Prometheus normalizer, cardinality controls, exemplar linking to traces, and initial dashboard targets.

Background / Why now:
- We receive metrics from multiple sources: runtime OTLP exporters, node-level Prometheus scrapers, and some third-party integrations. Each source has different label schemas and histogram formats.
- Current dashboards have inconsistent per-model latency numbers (mismatched buckets, label names, and missing token-rate signals), which blocks accurate SLO computation and incident triage.
- Upcoming Dedicated and Private tenants require tighter SLO observability and lower per-tenant metric cost.

Goals:
- Ingest OTLP metrics and Prometheus scrape data into a single stream and normalize label keys (model_name, model_variant, deployment_environment, sequence_length_bucket, kv_cache_hit).
- Convert varied histogram formats into a consistent Prometheus summary+histogram pair where appropriate, preserving exemplar mapping to traces.
- Emit derived KPIs: per-model p50/p95/p99 latency, per-model token throughput (tokens/s), per-model error-rate (5xx or delta between expected tokens vs produced).
- Apply cardinality reduction rules: bucketize sequence length, limit model_version label to family-level for high-card keys, and drop low-value free-form labels.
- Provide a controlled rollout with canary tenants and dashboard updates.

Non-goals:
- Full rearchitect of existing telemetry pipeline (that may be follow-up). This ticket focuses on the normalization/muxing layer and downstream metrics contract.

Design notes / decisions made:
- Architecture: Introduce a stateless metrics-muxer service that subscribes to OTLP/OTLP-gRPC and accepts Prometheus remote_write. It performs label normalization, computes derived metrics via streaming transforms, and forwards to the Metrics Gateway (ingest) and long-term storage.
- Exemplar linking: We will map latency histogram exemplars to trace IDs using the OTel exemplar extension. The muxer will preserve exemplar->trace id and attach model_name/model_variant so dashboards can link to traces.
- Cardinality policy: sequence_length -> buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512,513+]; model_version will be rewritten to model_family where model_family only changes on major architecture differences. Free-form prompt hashes are dropped by default.
- Histograms: For downstream consumers that require summarized values, the muxer will emit both histogram buckets (for Prometheus histogram queries) and a precomputed quantile summary for quick SLO checks.
- Backpressure & resiliency: The muxer will buffer up to N seconds of metrics and use an adaptive backoff when Metrics Gateway is unavailable.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- schema: add normalized label set document and publish to internal telemetry-schema repo (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-schema/pull/84).
- service: implement otlp ingest, promremote_write receiver, transform pipeline, exemplar passthrough (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-muxer).
- e2e: add integration tests that feed mixed OTLP/prometheus payloads and assert normalized outputs.
- dashboards: update latency/error dashboards and add per-model SLO panel + tokens/s panel (Grafana board id TBD).
- rollout: canary on infra-testing tenant, then 5 pilot customers, full rollout behind feature flag.

Progress / updates:
- 2025-11-05: Initial design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/metrics-muxer-design (draft). Feedback from Observability PMs collected.
- 2025-11-07: PR created for telemetry-schema changes (PR #84). Waiting on schema owner sign-off (@Ravi Patel).
- 2025-11-09: Prototype receiver implemented and running in dev cluster; can successfully normalize model_name/model_variant labels for synthetic OTLP traces.
- 2025-11-11: Added exemplar pass-through proof-of-concept and validated linking to traces in Staging (trace ids preserved in exported metrics).

Open questions / blockers:
- Cardinality threshold: what is the acceptable per-tenant time-series budget? Need agreement with cost/infra team.
- Security review: We are adding a service that ingests tenant metrics; requires review for PII leakage (prompt hashes) and KMS access for any encrypted payloads.
- Downstream contract: Will Alerts reference the new precomputed quantile summary or rely on raw histograms? Need SRE buy-in.

Acceptance criteria:
- Muxer receives mixed OTLP/prometheus payloads and emits normalized metrics with the agreed label set in staging for test tenants.
- Exemplars are preserved and map to trace IDs in at least 90% of test cases.
- Per-model p95 and tokens/s metrics consistently match runtime calculation within 5% for synthetic workloads.
- Dashboards updated and validated with on-call; alerting rules reviewed.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: deploy muxer to dev/staging and run integration tests for a week.
- Week 2: enable canary for infra-testing tenant (monitor time-series cardinality, CPU).
- Week 3: expand to 5 pilot tenants behind feature flag.
- Week 4: full rollout if pilot metrics are within cost/SLO targets.

Next steps (short):
- Resolve schema PR comments from @Ravi Patel and finalize label whitelist.
- Security to perform PII sweep on sample payloads (request ticket to security-assess queue).
- Wire up canary feature flag and prepare runbook for the first pilot.

Notes from reviewers:
- @Leila Moreno (SRE): "Agree with exemplar linking; we need to ensure the muxer doesn't drop exemplars under high write load."
- @Jason Park (Infra Cost): "Please add telemetry on series cardinality emitted per minute per tenant so we can measure budget impact."
